$comment: Rung 1 of the trust ladder: hand-verified values that beat every automated source. Every row with `vendorVerified` carries the `verifiedUrl` that was actually read, and the date it was read — that is what makes the claim checkable rather than merely asserted. Verification passes, what each covered and what each could NOT reach are recorded in `$verificationPasses` below; that is the field to read before assuming a row was checked. `capabilityIndex` is an illustrative 0-100 placeholder used only for the value map's Y axis - it is NOT a benchmark score, models without one are simply not plotted, and the UI says so.
$displayNames: Some entries carry a `displayName` and nothing else. Those are NOT price claims — they deliberately omit `vendorVerified`, so the rate and its provenance keep coming from whichever source the trust ladder chose. They exist because upstream ids get title-cased into names like `GPT 5`, `O3 Mini` and `Qwen3 Vl 235b A22b Instruct`, and since every model now has a public page those strings are its <h1> and its search-result title. A name is presentation; correcting one must not quietly upgrade a price to `vendor`.
$coverage: The catalog tracks what the automated feed carries. Vendors ship models before LiteLLM catalogues them — Z.ai published GLM-5.2 and GLM-5-Turbo on 2026-08-02 while the feed had neither — and the deliberate answer is to wait rather than hand-add. An override with a full `pricing` block CAN create a model the feed lacks, but that price is then frozen: no feed row exists to correct it, so it silently rots. Seeding from OpenRouter instead would publish a reseller's price as the vendor's, which for these providers runs 20-50% adrift. Missing a model for a few days costs less than publishing a number that is wrong and cannot self-correct. New models arrive on their own the morning the feed catches up.
$scope: These are standard-tier, global-endpoint list prices in USD. Not modelled: regional/data-residency premiums (OpenAI and Anthropic both charge 1.1x), fast/priority tiers, server-side tool call fees, fine-tuning, and negotiated volume discounts. The UI states this boundary rather than implying the figure is a whole invoice.
$timeOfDay: DeepSeek V4 publishes peak and off-peak rates but the current schema has no time-of-day tier. PromptSpend uses the higher peak rate so an estimate cannot silently understate the bill; off-peak usage can cost 50% less. Revisit this conservative representation when the engine can model a schedule explicitly.
$verificationPass20260812: First-party rendered pricing tables cleared four standing feed-versus-reseller flags without freezing matching base rates: Qwen 3.7 Max at the International/Singapore rate, Qwen3 Next 80B Instruct, Qwen3 VL 235B Instruct, and MiniMax M2.5. MiniMax also publishes a $0.375/M prompt-cache write rate absent from the feed; that modifier alone is overridden. This evidence was reconciled into the current catalog on 2026-08-16 from the reviewed PR #65 rather than merging its stale generated artifacts.
$verificationPass20260905: The last hand pass, and the reason it is the last. Sixteen rows verified together on 2026-08-03 (six Claude, nine OpenAI, Gemini 3.5 Flash — all provenance-only) crossed the 30-day rule together on 2026-09-05 and were re-read against their three pages that morning: every figure the catalog carries for them matched, so only lastVerified moved. Nothing automated had ever re-read a page behind an override before; from this date scripts/verify-vendors.ts does it every morning ahead of the sync (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Why the vendors' own pages are re-read every morning'). It moves a date only when the page agrees, raises vendor-page-mismatch when it does not, and never writes a price. The same pass retired Kimi K2.5's provenance and marked it and Mistral Medium 3 legacy — see their notes.

models.$note: Confirmed on 2026-09-02 against Anthropic's own pricing page: $10 base input, $50 output, $12.50 for a 5-minute cache write, and a $0.25 cache hit. THE CACHE-HIT RATE IS THE TRAP HERE and is why this row records a price rather than provenance alone: every other Claude model reads a cache hit at 0.1x base input, which would make it $1.00 — the figure its sibling Claude Fable 5 correctly carries. Anthropic's page footnotes an exception: "Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are priced at 0.025x the base input price." Deriving this one from the house multiplier instead of reading the footnote would overstate cached reads fourfold. The batch table reconciles independently at $5/$25, exactly the recorded 50%. Capability score 90: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 53 (read 2026-10-24), mapped onto this scale through four existing rows that also appear there. The older Claude Fable 5 still carries 100, which that index does not support; they should be rescored together.

Added 2026-09-29 to correct the generated name "Claude Opus 5 5" and record the vendor figures the feed lacks. Read against Anthropic's pricing page (the .md twin) on 2026-09-29: base input $4 / MTok, 5m cache writes $5, 1h cache writes $8, cache hits $0.20 (the page notes 0.05x base input), output $20. Batch is the standard 50%. Fast mode ($8/$40) is a separate speed tier and is not modelled. Context 1M and max output 128K per the Claude API model reference. capabilityIndex is the illustrative placeholder, set one above Claude Opus 5, which it succeeds at a lower price.

The $2/$10 introductory window ran through 2026-08-31 with a planned step-up to $3/$15; the vendor cancelled it — on 2026-09-01 the pricing page stated the introductory rate "is now the standard price" and the increase "will not occur" — so the base price was rewritten to $2/$10 and the intro block removed the same morning. Recording the in-force rate as THE price is the specific trap here (it flattened this very window away once, on 2026-08-16): it reads correct on the day it is written, the weekly audit still says `agree` because LiteLLM lags the same way, and the row then silently misprices from the moment the window closes. An intro rate must always be written as `intro` + `until`, never as the base `pricing`; fold it into base only when the vendor retires the window, as here.
